rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The worksheet gives no amount for married filing separately, which cannot take the deduction; the project enters zero there and the second enters $85,000. Neither reaches Schedule 1 line 21: sli.deduction is zero for married filing separately.
Ruling: equivalent; project retained. Line 6 is used only when line 4 is more than line 5 (line 8 skips it otherwise), where the signed difference and the floored one are the same.

Ruling: equivalent; project retained. The project skips to zero when line 4 is not more than line 5, as the worksheet says; the second always applies the ratio, which then has a part of zero or less, and prorate keeps the ratio at 0 or more, so it also gives zero (the same argument as the classified mutant on sli.line8).
Ruling: equivalent; project retained. Line 8 never exceeds line 1: prorate's ratio is at most 1.000 (Lean lemma prorate_le_amount), so the floor at zero never applies.

Ruling: equivalent; project retained. The second omits the 'interest more than zero' guard; with no interest line 1 and line 9 are zero, so the value is the same, and the project's guard keeps a filer without student loan interest from being asked whether they are claimed as a dependent. The eligibility tests (not married filing separately, not claimed as a dependent) agree.

Ruling: interface gap; i1040gi p. 98, Schedule 1, line 21 (the conditions for the deduction). The reply's two tests are the project's (a filing status other than married filing separately; no one on the return claimed as a dependent, person.sav_claimed) and it gives worksheet line 9 as the project does. It lacks the project's first alternative, $0 when no interest was paid (sli.interest zero), so it reads person.sav_claimed on returns with no student loan interest. The earlier rulings on this line found earlier replies to lack the dependent test; this reply has it. Re-reviewed because sli.interest was reworded (the older "(or your spouse if filing jointly)" in the eligible-student list is now the one spouse phrase; wording only, no expression changed). executable-triage-v2 (`.transcription/triage/2025/sli.json`, pass 970c08bc396c; 1,767 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 40 partial records): 1,759 of 2,307 comparisons agree; differences by kind {"candidate-refuses": 331, "candidate-unknown": 208, "project-unknown": 9}; on completed returns 101 candidate-unknown (on the six the record lists the project is $0 and the reply is unknown for person.sav_claimed); no value difference. The other differences are on refused or incomplete returns. No change to the data.

Ruling: model error; same point as the earlier rulings on this line. i1040gi p. 98, Line 21, among the conditions for the deduction: "You, or your spouse if filing jointly, aren't claimed as a dependent on someone else's" 2025 tax return. The reply gives worksheet line 9 on every return not married filing separately and has no test that the filer or the spouse is claimed as a dependent (its note says it found no input that asks it; the project reads person.sav_claimed). On completed returns where a person on the return is claimed the project enters zero and the reply the worksheet amount: 4 completed value differences, the recorded witnesses mutation.t2.sli.qss_divisor ($2,045.00 against $0.00; person[taxpayer].sav_claimed yes), stage11.sli.claimed, stage11.sli.spouse_claimed and stage16.sd.line17_no_skips_19. Triage executable-triage-v2 (`.transcription/triage/2025/sli.json`, pass e9feb0fa0109; 1,767 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026): 1,844 of 1,893 in-scope comparisons agree; differences by kind {"candidate-refuses": 381, "candidate-unknown": 36, "project-unknown": 8, "value": 5}; the candidate refusals are on its sa.excluded_income declaration and on refusals reaching the line from other forms, the fifth value difference is on a refused record. The project line is retained.
